title: Skill execution contract
description: Plan 5.1. The companion 'skill.yaml' that sits beside a canonical SKILL.md and states trigger, non-triggers, invocation authority, prerequisites, inputs, outputs, allowed side effects, required capabilities, child operations, hard gates, budget, failure outcomes, provenance and tests. This file is package metadata, not a promise that a host recognises these keys (plan 5.1); adapters and the validator interpret it. A skill.yaml is configuration, not a durable run artifact, so it does not carry common's envelope and is absent from common.schema.json#/$defs/schema_id.

id.description: Equals the skill directory name and the catalog entry id (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 1).

invocation.description: U = user-invoked, only a human starts it; M = model-invoked (AGENTS.md, 'The invocation law'). A user-invoked skill may call model-invoked skills; it may never call another user-invoked skill.

triggers.description: Concrete situations that should start this skill.

non_triggers.description: Concrete situations that must not start this skill. Plan 10 requires a negative-activation case for every skill, so this is never empty.

prerequisites.description: What must already hold before the skill runs: an approved artifact, an open review run, a configured tracker.

entrypoints.description: Named entrypoints. A public entrypoint is started by a human; a phase operation is started by a delegated controller only under a runner-validated grant (plan 7.1, AGENTS.md). Where the host cannot validate a grant, the entrypoint stops for explicit invocation rather than reproducing a forbidden command's effect.

operation.description: The shared phase operation this entrypoint runs, when one exists.

requires.description: Capabilities needed by this entrypoint beyond the skill-level 'requires'.

stops_without_grant.description: True when the host cannot validate the required grant and the entrypoint must stop for explicit invocation (plan 7.1).

allOf.description: A user-startable entrypoint cannot run on a grant alone; a grant-only entrypoint cannot be offered as a slash command.
An entrypoint that may run under delegation names the shared phase operation it runs, so the public wrapper and the controller use one protocol rather than two pipelines (plan 7.1).

requires.description: Host capabilities this skill cannot run without. A host that cannot supply one exposes the skill in guided mode rather than silently weakening the contract (plan 1.2).

schema.description: The artifact schema this output validates against, when the output is a durable artifact.

placement.description: Marks an output that is a knowledgebase document page: published through the knowledgebase adapter's `publishArtifact` under a `kb-document` placement (adapters/knowledgebase/CONTRACT.md). Run artifacts are marked by `schema` instead, so no other value is needed here.

kb_kind.description: The kind a `kb-document` output is published as. One of the knowledgebase's nine kinds; ADR-0001 §3 fixes which kinds each skill may write.

then.description: A KB document is a curated page, not a schema-bound run artifact (docs/decisions/0001-kb-document-vocabulary.md §2).

side_effects.description: Every effect this skill may cause. An effect absent here is a contract violation, not an omission.

child_operations.description: Phase operations this skill may start under a runner-validated grant (plan 7.1).

model_operations.description: Model-authority phase operations this skill may start (policies/invocation.yaml, authority: model). They run on no grant, so they are kept apart from child_operations, whose entries must be runner-delegable. Each must name this skill in its callable_by.

child_skills.description: Skills this skill may start directly. A user-invoked skill may list only model-invoked skills here; the check is an invocation-graph walk because the child's own invocation lives in the child's file (AGENTS.md, 'The invocation law').

packs.description: Packs that may attach while this skill runs. A pack adds constraints and review lenses; it never starts a phase (plan 3).

references.description: On-demand reference packs. Progressive disclosure is the mechanism that keeps the body under the line budget (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 2).

roles.description: Role prompts this skill seats. Roles are never individually invocable.

constraints.description: Named boolean constraints the skill asserts, e.g. reviewers-may-edit-source: false, author-may-approve-own-change: false (plan 5.1). A constraint is a contract the validator and the adapter check, not prose.

limits.description: Caps this skill enforces itself, e.g. fix-cycles: 2, rounds: 5, turns: 4. Values are counts, never currency and never a consumption ladder.

budget.description: Budgets are handed in by the runner; this package enforces only the cap it was handed (plan 7.2, AGENTS.md). The skill declares which of its limits it enforces and never computes or names a provider cost.

hard_gates.description: Conditions that stop the skill outright rather than degrading it, e.g. 'nothing is implemented before a human approves the direction'.

failure_outcomes.description: How the skill ends when it does not complete. Every status in common's operation_status that the skill can return must appear here with its meaning.

packaging.description: What the packager generates for a host bundle. Canonical SKILL.md frontmatter carries only Agent Skills spec keys (name, description, optionally license and metadata); the host keys below are GENERATED from this file and hand-writing one into a canonical SKILL.md is a validation failure (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 1). Declaring the intent here is the reason the packager can emit them at all.

disable-model-invocation.description: Emitted true for a user-invoked skill. Not portable across hosts (plan 1.3); an adapter that cannot express it must expose the skill in guided mode.

allowed-tools.description: Pre-approval, not a restrictive sandbox (plan 1.3, primary sources S1 and S2). It never stands in for a capability the host does not enforce.

hosts.description: Adapters that can carry this skill, and the semantics each one cannot enforce.

tests.description: Behavioral cases (plan 4, plan 10). Every skill carries at least one positive activation case and one negative activation case; a folder with no behavioral test is not a capability.

body.description: Line budget for the canonical SKILL.md: 150 lines, hard cap 300 (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 2). Longer material goes behind references/.

allOf.description: ADR-0007 reserves standing-start authority for autopilot alone.

A user-invoked skill declares disable-model-invocation: true as the record of its class; a model-invoked skill never does (catalog.yaml field notes, AGENTS.md). The declaration is not emitted on any host (docs/decisions/0003-model-invocation.md).
A user-invoked skill exposes at least one entrypoint a human can start, so the slash command is the real way in rather than a side door (AGENTS.md, 'The invocation law').

not.description: Fails when every entrypoint is model-invoked, which would leave a user-invoked skill with no human way in.

allOf.description: A skill that writes outside the workspace declares the matching capability, so an adapter that cannot supply it refuses the skill instead of running it half-enforced (plan 1.2).

provenance.description: AGENTS.md, authoring rule 3. 'donor' means at least one adapted file with a provenance/adaptations.yaml row of the form donor@commit:path that exists at the pin. 'conversation' means no donor implements it and carries a G:L locator instead; a fabricated source path is never acceptable (plan 1.4).

resolved_conflicts.description: Rows of policies/resolved-conflicts.yaml this file touches. Citing the ruling is mandatory wherever a skill touches one (AGENTS.md, authoring rule 4).
